faq:faq-sup-001.title: I feel really lonely since I became Muslim. Is that normal?
keyPoints: Cites a Yaqeen Institute survey of American converts: masjids, imams and Muslim friendships matter, and support is needed long after the Shahada
For loneliness that turns into hopelessness, gives 911 in an emergency, then 9-8-8 by call or text

faq:faq-sup-003.title: How do I know who I can trust for help?
keyPoints: Lists warning signs: asking for money, rushing you into marriage, demanding secrecy, cutting you off from family or other Muslims
Says 211 in Ontario is confidential and answered 24/7 by call or text 2-1-1, for housing, food or counselling
Advises trusting organisations with a public program page, office phone or email over individuals you just met

faq:faq-sup-004.title: Is there a program for new Muslims in Ottawa?
keyPoints: Says Islam Care Centre, 375 Somerset St. W, Ottawa, runs a free weekly Convert Care program for new Muslims
Says it meets every Wednesday at 6:00 pm; phone (613) 232-0210

faq:faq-sup-005.title: I went to the masjid and nobody talked to me. Did I do something wrong?
keyPoints: Quotes New Muslim Academy: communities are imperfect and your faith does not depend on how one group received you
Suggests a quieter time, introducing yourself to the office or imam, or trying another masjid

faq:faq-sup-007.title: Can I talk to a Muslim counsellor?
keyPoints: Naseeha Muslim youth helpline at 1 (866) 627-3342
Nisa Helpline for women and girls 14+ at +1 888 711 6472, 8 am to midnight Eastern (source is review-needed; its FAQ shows an older number)
Khalil Center (online, 416-901-2244) and Muslim Family Services of Ottawa (613-562-2273) named for professional counselling
Says none replace 911 or 9-8-8; advises checking a counsellor's registration with the provincial college

faq:faq-lif-001.title: How can I tell if food in a Canadian store is really halal?
keyPoints: Says a federal CFIA rule requires any label saying or suggesting 'halal' to name the certifying person or organisation
Names HMA and ISNA Canada Halal as common Ontario certifiers with different standards (no ISNA source attached)
Difference note: certifiers differ on machine slaughter and stunning

faq:faq-lif-002.title: What food is actually forbidden for Muslims?
keyPoints: Lists from Quran 2:173: carrion, blood, pork and meat dedicated to other than Allah, plus the necessity exception
Cites Quran 5:90 for intoxicants
Says vegetables, fruit, grains, eggs and fish are generally fine and some cheeses use animal enzymes
Difference note: seafood and some animals differ between the schools

faq:faq-lif-003.title: Is vanilla extract or food with a little alcohol in the ingredients okay?
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school (via SeekersGuidance) allows non-wine alcohol in vanilla if not used to intoxicate and the amount cannot intoxicate
Says alcohol-free vanilla is the more careful option and many other scholars avoid any added alcohol
Cites Sahih Muslim 2002: every intoxicant is forbidden

faq:faq-lif-004.title: Do I need to avoid gelatin?
keyPoints: Says the Shafi'i school holds pork gelatin stays forbidden; Hanafi, Maliki and one Hanbali view accept full transformation (istihala) more broadly
Cites AMJA fatwa 1889 accepting the transformation argument for gelatin
Cites AMJA fatwa 84728: a medicine or vaccine containing gelatin may be taken when there is no alternative

faq:faq-lif-005.title: My family serves regular supermarket meat. Can I eat it?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 5:5 for the view that meat of Christians and Jews (People of the Book) is allowed
Cites AMJA fatwa 80178: no need to ask how meat was slaughtered when unknown, but not when known to be improperly slaughtered
Says many scholars and Canadian certifiers accept only zabiha meat

faq:faq-lif-006.title: We share a kitchen and the family cooks pork. Are the dishes and pans okay for me?
keyPoints: Attributes to Shaykh Faraz Rabbani (SeekersGuidance) that washing once, by hand or dishwasher, with or without soap, purifies dishes used for pork
Calls over-checking baseless misgivings (waswasa); cites Bukhari 39 'the religion is easy'
Difference note says this follows the Hanafi school and some schools are stricter about pork

faq:faq-lif-007.title: Can I ask my employer or school for time to pray?
keyPoints: Says Ontario Human Rights Code undue hardship is limited to cost, outside funding, and health and safety; sincerity is the test
Says federally regulated employers (banks, airlines, Canada Post, federal departments) fall under the Canadian Human Rights Act
Says Quebec's laicity law bars listed public-sector roles from religious symbols and limits prayer in listed public bodies (statute source is review-needed)
Says a prayer break incl. wudu takes about 10 to 15 minutes; suggests the Muslim Federal Employees Network managers' guide

faq:faq-lif-008.title: What about Friday prayer and fasting in Ramadan at work?
keyPoints: Says OHRC examples for Friday prayer include a longer lunch, staggered hours or making the time up
Says OHRC mentions working through lunch to leave early for breaking the fast, without loss of pay
Says you can ask for Eid off without being forced to use vacation days (lieu time, shift swaps)

faq:faq-lif-009.title: I live in Quebec. Are the rules different?
keyPoints: Says Bill 21 bars people in listed public-sector roles from wearing religious symbols such as a hijab at work
Says the law was expanded in 2025 and 2026: prayer in school buildings during class hours, subsidised daycare workers, public institutions
Says a Supreme Court of Canada challenge was heard in 2026

faq:faq-lif-010.title: My team socials are always at a bar. What do I do?
keyPoints: Cites Jami at-Tirmidhi 2801 (graded hasan) for not sitting at a table where alcohol is served
Says SeekersGuidance advises politely declining alcohol-centred gatherings and suggesting alternatives
Says scholars differ on events where alcohol is present but not the focus

faq:faq-lif-024.title: Do I have to stop shaking hands with people of the opposite sex?
keyPoints: Says most scholars of the four schools forbid handshakes between unrelated men and women; cites Aisha's report in Sahih Muslim 1866b
Says Egypt's Dar al-Ifta (fatwa 9383, source review-needed) lets a Muslim follow scholars who allow a handshake without desire
Cites AMJA fatwa 23202: explain it is respect, not disdain; if caught in an unavoidable moment, ask Allah's forgiveness
Difference note: the Hanafi and Hanbali schools allow it with elderly women

faq:faq-lif-025.title: I have tattoos from before Islam. Do I need to remove them?
keyPoints: Says pre-Islam tattoos need not be removed if removal is costly or harmful (AMJA fatwas 22996 and 82498)
Quotes Sahih al-Bukhari 1436: 'You became Muslim with all those good deeds'
Says tattoos need not be covered in prayer and may be uncovered in hot weather

faq:faq-lif-026.title: I already have a dog. Do I have to give it up?
keyPoints: Says scholars 'generally discourage' indoor pet dogs but allow working and guard dogs; confirm the wording of AMJA 77827 and the SeekersGuidance answer
Says the Maliki school is known for a more lenient view on dogs
Names service dogs and dogs owned by other family members as cases to take to a scholar

faq:faq-lif-027.title: Do I have to stop listening to music?
keyPoints: Says most of the four schools forbid instruments except the duff; cites Sahih al-Bukhari 5590 and notes its chain is discussed (mu'allaq)
Says Imam al-Ghazali and Egypt's Dar al-Ifta (fatwa 4866) allow clean music with conditions
Cites AMJA fatwa 77201: hearing music you did not choose is not held against you
Says singing with good words is fine

faq:faq-lif-028.title: I have a mortgage, credit card or car loan with interest. What now?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 2:275 (interest forbidden, trade permitted) and 2:278-279 (give up outstanding interest)
Advises keeping up existing payments, paying credit cards in full each month and avoiding new interest-based debt
Says many scholars, incl. SeekersGuidance teachers, say avoid conventional mortgages for scholar-board-checked Islamic financing
Says Egypt's Dar al-Ifta (fatwa 5875, about a UK mortgage) allows a bank home loan as a sale (murabaha)

faq:faq-lif-029.title: Are lottery tickets, sports betting or office pools okay?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 5:90 listing gambling with intoxicants
Says lottery tickets, casino games, sports betting and paid office pools are all gambling
Difference note: scholars differ on free draws; AMJA 1645 says a free draw with no payment is not gambling

faq:faq-lif-030.title: I smoke or vape. Do I have to quit right away?
keyPoints: Says many contemporary scholars hold smoking forbidden (haram) or strongly disliked and others disliked (makruh), per SeekersGuidance
Says cannabis is treated like alcohol because it intoxicates
Points to Health Canada and your doctor for quitting support (no Health Canada source attached); vaping is not addressed separately

faq:faq-lif-011.title: Do I still have to respect my parents if they are not Muslim?
keyPoints: Quotes Quran 31:15 as 'keep their company in this world courteously'; check wording against The Clear Quran ('keep them company')
Quotes Sahih al-Bukhari 2620: Asma bint Abi Bakr told 'Yes, keep good relation with her' about her non-Muslim mother
Cites Quran 60:8 on kindness and fairness to those who have not fought you

faq:faq-lif-012.title: I still live with my parents and they don't like my new practices. How do I handle it?
keyPoints: Attributes advice to Shaykh Abdullah Anik Misra (convert from Toronto, SeekersGuidance): firm on prayer and fasting, avoid debates, share only major rules
Suggests being vegetarian at home if needed and dressing neatly so family sees you are still you
Says if home is not safe, safety comes first; points to the red flags guide and the Government of Canada safety planning page

faq:faq-lif-013.title: Someone told me I should cut off my non-Muslim family. Is that true?
keyPoints: Says keeping family ties is required whatever relatives' religion (SeekersGuidance)
Cites the Prophet telling Asma bint Abi Bakr to keep good relations with her non-Muslim mother (Bukhari 2620)
Says contact with a harmful relative may be reduced; community pressure to cut off family is a warning sign

faq:faq-lif-014.title: I became Muslim but my husband or wife did not. What happens to my marriage?
keyPoints: Says a husband's marriage to a Christian or Jewish wife stays valid (SeekersGuidance 2019 Shafi'i answer; footnote adds a strict Shafi'i lineage condition)
Says AMJA Family Code art. 42: for a convert wife, intimacy stops and the marriage is suspended in iddah; continues if he converts, else she may end it
Says a Canadian civil marriage ends only through a court; difference note cites the European Council for Fatwa and Research allowing a wife to stay
Cites Yaqeen 2025 survey of 618 US converts: 29.6% of married men and 13% of married women had a non-Muslim spouse

faq:faq-lif-015.title: Can I keep my non-Muslim friends?
keyPoints: Says befriending non-Muslims is neither forbidden nor disliked (SeekersGuidance)
Reads Quran 5:51 as about alliances that harm the Muslim community, not friendship (no Quran 5:51 entry attached; relies on SeekersGuidance)
Cites Quran 60:8; says in one survey most converts made friends at their local masjid (Yaqeen 2025)

faq:faq-sup-012.title: People keep telling me I need to get married soon. Do I have to?
keyPoints: Says no one has the right to rush you into marriage; advises talking to a qualified imam about your own situation
Says threats or control over who you see are unacceptable; in danger, call 9-1-1

faq:faq-fnd-001.title: What do the words of the Shahada actually mean?
keyPoints: Transliterates 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah' as 'I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah'
Transliterates 'Wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasul Allah' as 'and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'
Says the Prophet was human, not divine, and the final messenger; knowing the core meaning is enough to start

faq:faq-fnd-002.title: I said the Shahada on my own, with nobody there. Am I really Muslim?
keyPoints: Says witnesses are not needed for a Shahada to be valid between you and Allah (SeekersGuidance)
Says witnesses and a certificate are for community recognition, e.g. a masjid marriage or Hajj

faq:faq-fnd-003.title: Do I need a Shahada certificate?
keyPoints: Says a certificate is not needed to be Muslim but may be needed for a masjid marriage or Umrah and Hajj applications
Says some masjids issue imam-signed certificates on request (source example: Ummah Masjid, Halifax)

faq:faq-fnd-004.title: What are the five pillars of Islam?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 8 and Muslim 16a: 'Islam is built on five'
Describes zakat as a yearly charity for those with enough savings and Hajj as once in a lifetime for those able (Muslim 1337)
Says zakat and Hajj apply only when circumstances require; prayer is the next pillar after the Shahada

faq:faq-fnd-005.title: I have said the Shahada. What comes next?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 1395 / Muslim 19a: a companion sent to teach was told to teach the Shahada first, then the five daily prayers
Says many scholars advise ghusl after becoming Muslim; difference note says schools differ on required vs recommended (Abu Dawud 355)
Suggests the order: understand the Shahada, learn wudu, then one short prayer

faq:faq-fnd-006.title: Do I have to do all five pillars straight away?
keyPoints: Says zakat applies only once savings pass a set minimum (nisab) and Hajj once in a lifetime if physically and financially able
Says fasting starts when Ramadan arrives and the focus in the first weeks is faith and prayer

faq:faq-fnd-007.title: What do Muslims believe? What are the six articles of faith?
keyPoints: Cites the hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim 8a): belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and Allah's decree of good and bad
Says angels, prophets and a day of judgement will feel familiar to those raised Christian or Jewish

faq:faq-fnd-008.title: What is shirk, and why do Muslims take it so seriously?
keyPoints: Defines shirk as giving any part of worship, or any quality belonging only to God, to someone or something else
Counts 'calling on someone for help beyond human ability' as worship; confirm the wording fits mainstream Sunni views on istighatha
Says the Quran calls shirk the gravest wrong (31:13)
Says Allah forgives anyone who turns away from shirk (8:38, Muslim 121); Quran 4:48 also cited

faq:faq-fnd-009.title: I used to pray to Jesus. Was that wrong, and will I be punished for it?
keyPoints: Quotes Quran 19:30: Jesus says 'I am the servant of Allah'
Says prayer is directed to Allah alone, not to Jesus, Mary or the saints, and not 'in Jesus's name'
Says past acts are forgiven: Islam wipes out what came before (Muslim 121) and Quran 8:38

faq:faq-fnd-012.title: What happens to the sins I committed before I became Muslim?
keyPoints: Quotes Sahih Muslim 121 (Amr ibn al-As): 'Are you not aware that Islam wipes out all the previous misdeeds?'
Cites Quran 25:70: for those who repent, believe and do good, Allah replaces bad deeds with good
Advises repaying what is owed to people; difference note says scholars discuss whether such rights are cancelled

faq:faq-fnd-013.title: Will the good things I did before Islam count for anything?
keyPoints: Quotes Bukhari 1436 / Muslim 123a: Hakim ibn Hizam told 'You became Muslim with all those good deeds'
Says past charity and kindness to family are not lost

faq:faq-fnd-014.title: I have made mistakes since becoming Muslim. How do I repent?
keyPoints: Gives three parts of repentance (tawbah): regret, stopping and sincere intention not to return; wrongs to people should be put right
Paraphrases Sahih Muslim 2747: Allah is more pleased with repentance than a traveller who finds his lost camel
Says you can repent at any time, in any language, and slipping again does not close the door

faq:faq-fnd-015.title: I believe, but I am not praying five times a day yet. Am I still a Muslim?
keyPoints: Says you are Muslim through belief and the Shahada while working towards the five daily prayers
Says scholars who guide converts advise doing what you can without deliberately neglecting prayer (SeekersGuidance)
Difference note: scholars differ on someone who abandons prayer altogether; the answer gives no ruling on that

faq:faq-fnd-016.title: Do I have to change my name?
keyPoints: Says most companions kept their names; a change is needed only if the meaning goes against Islam (e.g. 'servant of the Messiah') or is bad
Says you should keep your family name because Islam values connection to your father's lineage
Cites Sahih Muslim 2139 on changing a name with a bad meaning

faq:faq-fnd-017.title: Do I have to be circumcised? (for men)
keyPoints: Says circumcision is not needed to become Muslim and the Shahada is valid either way
Says schools differ: the Maliki school treats it as sunnah, other sources as required; cites Bukhari 5889 (fitra)
Advises an adult to talk to a doctor as well as a qualified scholar before deciding

faq:faq-fnd-018.title: Do I have to tell people that I am Muslim?
keyPoints: Says announcing your conversion is not a condition of being Muslim (NewMuslims.com)
Says if telling someone could put you at risk, safety comes first; points to the family guide's safety resources

faq:faq-fnd-019.title: Do I have to know Arabic to be Muslim?
keyPoints: Says Arabic is not a condition of Islam and most Muslims are not Arabic speakers
Says dua can be in any language, while the five prayers include short Arabic passages, mainly al-Fatiha (IslamQA 20815)
preCheckFlags: Says 'see the next question' for ways to pray while learning, but the next Foundations question is faq-fnd-022 (is the Shahada enough); the relevant one is faq-pry-006

faq:faq-fnd-022.title: Is saying the Shahada enough, or do I need to do something else to become Muslim?
keyPoints: Says sincerely believing and saying the Shahada makes you Muslim; no ceremony, fee, certificate, name change or Arabic needed first
Cites Sahih al-Bukhari 128 on testifying sincerely

faq:faq-lrn-002.title: There is so much to learn. Where do I even start?
keyPoints: Paraphrases Bukhari 6464: the most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant, even if small
Recommends New Muslim Academy self-paced courses with student forums
Suggests an order: belief, Shahada and prayer; then Al-Fatihah and short chapters, their meaning, then fasting and daily life

faq:faq-lrn-006.title: How can I tell if an online source about Islam is reliable?
keyPoints: Says hadith are graded by their chain of narrators into grades such as sahih (authentic) and da'if (weak)
Says AI tools can invent references; recommends checking verses on Quran.com and hadith and their grades on Sunnah.com
Cites Quran 49:6 on checking news before acting on it
Warns against videos telling you to reject all teachers except one, and anything that makes you afraid or rushed

faq:faq-lrn-009.title: Should I sign up for a course? Which one?
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Academy: free, made for new Muslims, starts with wudu and prayer, needs a free account
Recommends SeekersGuidance free Level One live classes
Warns about courses asking for money up front, pushing you to cut off other teachers, or wanting unnecessary personal details

faq:faq-wor-027.title: Do I have to go on Hajj right away?
keyPoints: Says Hajj is required once in a lifetime for those physically and financially able; Quran 3:97 ties it to ability
Says Umrah, the smaller pilgrimage, is a separate act
Difference note: schools differ on whether Hajj must be done as soon as you are able or may be delayed

faq:faq-wor-028.title: How do I book Hajj or Umrah safely from Canada?
keyPoints: Says Government of Canada travel advice currently says avoid non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia (source checked 25 September 2026)
Says Hajj needs a Hajj visa via the Saudi Nusuk platform or its authorized providers; Umrah can be done on other visa types
Advises reporting suspected Hajj fraud (cheap or guaranteed places, cash deposits, pressure) to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre

faq:faq-wor-029.title: As a woman, can I go on Umrah alone, and what if my period starts?
keyPoints: Says Saudi rules let women of any age travel for Hajj or Umrah without a mahram, per the Government of Canada
Says a woman on her period does everything except tawaf, done once clean, as the Prophet told Aisha (Bukhari 1650, a Hajj report)
Check how 'everything except tawaf' applies to Umrah, where sa'i and cutting the hair come after tawaf
Difference note: schools differ on needing a mahram; leaving before becoming clean for tawaf is a question for a scholar

faq:faq-lif-016.title: Can I still spend Christmas with my family?
keyPoints: Says many scholars allow attending family Christmas without joining religious rites; SeekersGuidance calls it part of keeping family ties
Difference note cites AMJA 77225 (decline a friend's dinner), Islamweb (visit family at other times) and IslamQA (stricter)
Says where alcohol is served views differ and the stricter view says not to attend

faq:faq-lif-017.title: Can I give or accept Christmas presents?
keyPoints: Says accepting gifts is widely considered fine and a Sunnah practice (no hadith attached for this)
Says SeekersGuidance allows giving presents to family in December to strengthen ties
Says an AMJA scholar allows declining a gift tied directly to religious ritual; some scholars advise no Christmas tree at home

faq:faq-lif-018.title: Someone says 'Merry Christmas' to me. What should I say back?
keyPoints: Says Egypt's Dar al-Ifta (fatwa 6710) allows congratulating non-Muslims on their occasions without agreeing with their beliefs
Attributes to Shaykh Jamaal Zarabozo for AMJA (fatwa 85952) advice not to say 'Merry Christmas' and to reply warmly in another way

faq:faq-lif-019.title: Is Thanksgiving okay?
keyPoints: Says SeekersGuidance teachers see Canadian Thanksgiving as a national, family occasion and permit attending the family dinner
Says some AMJA scholars (fatwas 76974 and 22994) say Muslims should not celebrate it

faq:faq-lif-020.title: What about Halloween, especially for my kids?
keyPoints: Says most scholars whose answers were checked advise not joining Halloween because of its origins
Attributes to Shaykh Faraz Rabbani (answering a parent in Canada) giving children treats or an outing instead
Cites AMJA 83012 (convert mother): put that energy into the two Eids with sweets, gifts and dressing up
Difference note: handing out candy at the door is treated as a separate question

faq:faq-lif-021.title: Can I celebrate birthdays?
keyPoints: Says one AMJA scholar treats birthdays as social occasions, not explicitly forbidden, especially for children (AMJA 77128)
Says another AMJA scholar says not permissible and a SeekersGuidance teacher 'leans that way'; the source note says SeekersGuidance reports both views

faq:faq-lif-022.title: Can I go to church with my family for a wedding, a funeral, Easter or Christmas?
keyPoints: Says joining another religion's worship is a clear line; SeekersGuidance says quietly do not take part in religious activities
Says Dar al-Ifta (fatwa 5935) and an AMJA scholar (78565) allow attending a relative's funeral, even in a church
Says SeekersGuidance Hanafi answers allow the family gathering but not the church service without strong need; IslamQA is strict
Says the only wedding-specific source found (IslamQA 6992) is strict

faq:faq-lif-023.title: There will be alcohol at the family party. Should I still go?
keyPoints: Says scholars generally advise against sitting where alcohol is served (Tirmidhi 2801, graded hasan)
Says SeekersGuidance calls a gathering built around alcohol no place for a believer
Describes converts sitting with non-drinkers, bringing their own drinks and leaving before things get rowdy

faq:faq-wor-030.title: Do I have to do qurbani for Eid al-Adha?
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school holds qurbani required for those above the zakat threshold; most other scholars say strongly recommended
Says the sacrifice is after the Eid al-Adha prayer (Bukhari 5545) and the meat is shared, including with people in need
Names Islamic Relief Canada as arranging qurbani for donors
Cites Quran 22:37; difference note on not cutting hair and nails beforehand (Muslim 1977c)

faq:faq-wor-001.title: Do I pray during my period, and do I have to make those prayers up later?
keyPoints: Says no prayer during a period or post-childbirth bleeding and no make-up; attributes Aisha's report (Bukhari 321, Muslim 335c) to 'the wives of the Prophet'
Says prayer resumes from the next prayer once bleeding ends and ghusl is done
Says a prayer may be owed if its time began before bleeding or the period ends before the time is over (AMJA 78935)

faq:faq-wor-002.title: If my period comes during Ramadan, do I still fast? Do I owe those days?
keyPoints: Says a fast becomes void if a period begins before sunset; missed days are made up one for one, ideally before the next Ramadan
Cites Sahih Muslim 335c: make up missed fasts, not missed prayers
Difference note: if make-up is delayed past the next Ramadan without reason, some add fidyah and the Hanafi school does not

faq:faq-wor-003.title: Can I read or recite the Quran during my period?
keyPoints: Says Hanafi and Shafi'i schools bar reciting aloud during a period but allow listening, looking, reflecting and Quranic phrases as dua
Says the Maliki school allows recitation; some later scholars allow recitation from memory without touching a printed Quran
Says Tirmidhi 131, often quoted for the ban, is graded weak (no Sunnah.com entry attached; IslamQA 2564 notes it)

faq:faq-wor-004.title: Can I touch the Quran, or use a Quran app on my phone, during my period?
keyPoints: Says most scholars bar touching a printed Arabic Quran (mushaf) during a period; many allow holding it with a separate cover
Says a phone or tablet app is not a mushaf; AMJA gave this view for devices and tafsir books
Says the Hanafi school is stricter about touching printed translations and tafsir; AMJA 86681 permits touching the mushaf when needed
preCheckFlags: Difference note says NewMuslims.com allows touching translations, but no NewMuslims.com source is attached to this item

faq:faq-wor-005.title: Can I still make dua and dhikr while I am on my period?
keyPoints: Says dua and dhikr (SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar) are allowed at any time during a period
Says sending blessings on the Prophet, listening to the Quran and charity continue; schools checked allow Quranic verses said as dua

faq:faq-wor-006.title: Can I go to the masjid, a class, or Eid while on my period?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 324: women on their periods told to come out for Eid while staying away from the prayer rows
Says most schools say not to stay in the main prayer hall during a period; some scholars allow it
Says Abu Dawud 232 ('I do not make the mosque lawful for a menstruating woman') is graded weak by al-Albani
Says classrooms, halls and offices may not count as the masjid; ask the imam which rooms do

faq:faq-wor-007.title: How do I know my period has ended, and what do I do then?
keyPoints: Says the period ends when bleeding stops; check with a white cloth or pad for clear or white discharge or complete dryness
Describes ghusl as intention, washing, and water reaching the whole body and hair roots
Difference note: signs of purity and how to treat brown or yellow discharge differ by school

faq:faq-wor-008.title: I keep bleeding outside my normal period. Do I still pray?
keyPoints: Says bleeding outside the usual period or past the longest length is istihadah and does not stop prayer (Bukhari 306)
Says in the Hanafi school, when bleeding runs past ten days, the days beyond your usual length count as istihadah
Says an 'excused' person makes one wudu when each prayer time begins, lasting until it ends (Hanafi); other schools differ
Advises keeping a record of bleeding and seeing a doctor about the cause

faq:faq-wor-009.title: What about bleeding after giving birth?
keyPoints: Says bleeding after childbirth (nifas) follows period rules: no prayer or fasting, fasts made up, prayers not
Says many scholars give forty days as the usual maximum; if bleeding stops earlier, do ghusl and pray (Abu Dawud 311)
Advises new mothers to follow their doctor's or midwife's advice

faq:faq-wor-010.title: Is my period a sign that I am spiritually impure or less of a Muslim?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 305: the Prophet told Aisha, upset when her period came during Hajj, that it is written for all the daughters of Adam
Cites Bukhari 297: the Prophet rested his head in Aisha's lap and recited the Quran during her period
Says the break from prayer and fasting is a rule for a set time, not a judgement

faq:faq-sup-014.title: A mentor or teacher is making me uncomfortable. What can I do?
keyPoints: Lists mentor red flags: asking for money, meeting alone in private places, marriage pressure, asking for photos, secrecy
Says in danger or after a crime call 9-1-1 or the police; tell the program coordinator
Says people connected to Revert Guide can be reported through the get help page

faq:faq-pry-001.title: What are the five daily prayers called, and when do I pray them?
keyPoints: Gives windows: Fajr dawn to sunrise, Dhuhr until Asr, Asr until sunset, Maghrib until Isha, Isha until the middle of the night 'for most purposes'
Difference note: the Hanafi Asr starts later; schools differ on the latest time for Isha
Cites Quran 4:103 and 17:78 for prayer at fixed times

faq:faq-pry-002.title: How many units (rak'ahs) does each prayer have?
keyPoints: Says Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4: 17 obligatory units a day
Defines a rak'ah as one cycle of standing, bowing and two prostrations
Difference note: on a journey Dhuhr, Asr and Isha can be shortened to two

faq:faq-pry-003.title: Why do different apps and masjids show different prayer times?
keyPoints: Says ISNA uses 15 degrees and Muslim World League 18 degrees for Fajr
Says the Fiqh Council of North America finds no single method exact and suggests a few minutes of caution as a recommendation
Says differences between methods can exceed an hour in summer in Canada

faq:faq-pry-004.title: Which prayer time method should I use in Canada?
keyPoints: Says the Fiqh Council of North America recommended 13 degrees for Fajr and Isha in Canada
Says a newer FCNA article calls 15 degrees a good middle approximation; difference note says the two articles disagree
Mentions the Moonsighting Committee seasonal method; advises following your masjid's timetable

faq:faq-pry-005.title: I live far north and in summer Isha is very late and Fajr is very early. What do I do?
keyPoints: Says above roughly 48.5 degrees latitude the summer sky may not get dark enough for the 18-degree setting
Says methods use seasonal estimates or a portion of the night; ask your local masjid which timetable it follows

faq:faq-pry-006.title: I can't read or recite Arabic yet. Can I still pray?
keyPoints: Says Arabic remembrance phrases may replace unmemorised recitation; cites Abu Dawud 832 (hasan) and SeekersGuidance (valid for Hanafi and Shafi'i)
Check translations: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah ('There is no god but Allah'), Allahu Akbar ('Allah is greater')
Says all four schools recite al-Fatiha in Arabic in prayer though they differ on its legal status; cites Quran 2:286
Difference note: Hanafi accepts the meaning in your own language; Shafi'i uses dhikr, then silent standing; Maliki and Hanbali do not accept

faq:faq-pry-007.title: Can I say my prayer in English?
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school lets someone who cannot yet recite Arabic recite a translation of Quran verses in prayer
Says the Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools do not accept recitation in another language
Says SeekersGuidance calls short Arabic remembrance phrases the more cautious option, valid in the Hanafi and Shafi'i schools

faq:faq-pry-008.title: Can I read the words from a card or my phone while I pray?
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school counts reading from a Quran in prayer as strongly disliked; confirm against Hanafi texts that list it as invalidating (Abu Hanifa)
Difference note says the Shafi'i school lets a learner read al-Fatiha from a mushaf in prayer; no Shafi'i source is attached
Advises memorising short phrases first and using a card only outside prayer

faq:faq-pry-009.title: What is the simplest prayer I can start with this week?
keyPoints: Describes one rak'ah: face the qibla, say Allahu Akbar, say what you know, bow, stand, two prostrations with a sitting between
Cites Bukhari 757: the man who prayed badly was told to recite what he knew of the Quran and be calm in each position

faq:faq-pry-010.title: How do I build up from one rak'ah to the full five prayers?
keyPoints: Says pray all five daily prayers in a simple form while learning; the steps change what you say and add
Order: positions and phrases, Fajr (2 units), sitting and tashahhud, then 3- and 4-unit prayers, then al-Fatiha and a short surah
Says each step is a real prayer, not a rehearsal

faq:faq-pry-011.title: What do I say in each position of the prayer?
keyPoints: Check transliterations and translations: Subhana Rabbiyal Azim, Sami Allahu liman hamidah, Rabbana wa lakal hamd, Subhana Rabbiyal A'la
Says between prostrations say Rabbighfir li (My Lord, forgive me); ends with As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah to the right and left
Cites Abu Dawud 874 (bowing and prostration), Bukhari 3370 (blessings on the Prophet) and Bukhari 831 (tashahhud)

faq:faq-pry-017.title: Do I have to make up the prayers from before I became Muslim?
keyPoints: Says prayers from before becoming Muslim are not owed (difference note: scholars agree)
Says Hanafi scholars hold a convert who did not yet know prayer was obligatory need not make up that time

faq:faq-pry-018.title: I missed a prayer. What should I do now?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 597: whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when they remember
Suggests a teacher help set a small, steady make-up plan for many prayers missed since becoming Muslim
Difference note: schools differ on deliberately missed prayers and on sunnah prayers while making up

faq:faq-pry-019.title: I made a mistake in my prayer. Do I have to start again?
keyPoints: Says forgetting the rak'ah count or adding or missing a part is usually fixed by two prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw)
Says authentic reports place them both before (Muslim 571a) and after the closing salam (Bukhari 1226)

faq:faq-pry-020.title: I can't stand, bow or prostrate because of pain or disability. How do I pray?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 1117: pray standing, if unable then sitting, if unable then lying on your side
Says if you cannot prostrate, lower the head a little for bowing and more for prostration
Says a chair is allowed when needed (details differ by school); cites Quran 2:286

faq:faq-pry-021.title: Do women pray differently from men?
keyPoints: Says some schools teach women to keep the arms and body closer together in bowing and prostration
Says a SeekersGuidance scholar explains these differences concern the best way, not whether the prayer counts
Difference note: some scholars teach no difference in form

faq:faq-pry-025.title: Different videos show different hand positions. Who is right?
keyPoints: Says the four schools differ on where the hands rest when standing and on raising the hands before bowing
Check the attached sources (NMA Salah for Beginners PDF, SeekersGuidance men-and-women answer) cover these differences between schools

faq:faq-pry-026.title: Why do Muslims pray five times a day?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 4:103 (fixed times), 29:45 (keeps a person from wrongdoing) and 2:45 (seek help through patience and prayer)
Calls prayer the second pillar of Islam

faq:faq-pry-027.title: Is there a good video to watch someone pray from start to finish?
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Academy's short course with a video demonstration of wudu and prayer
Recommends Sheikh Assim al-Hakeem's official channel lecture on the Prophet's prayer (YouTube T4auGhmeBlw); confirm suitability

faq:faq-pry-012.title: Do I have to do a full-body wash (ghusl) because I became Muslim?
keyPoints: Says Hanafi and Shafi'i schools hold ghusl on accepting Islam recommended, required if already in a state needing ghusl (e.g. after intimacy)
Says the Maliki and Hanbali schools are reported to require it in all cases; difference note says sources differ on the Hanbali position
Cites Abu Dawud 355 (sahih): the Prophet told a man who accepted Islam to bathe

faq:faq-pry-013.title: Is my Shahada valid if I haven't done ghusl yet?
keyPoints: Says the two testimonies said with conviction make a person Muslim and ghusl is not a condition of that (Islamweb fatwa 11140)
Advises taking ghusl when you can and before your first prayer

faq:faq-pry-014.title: What breaks my wudu?
keyPoints: Says scholars agree using the toilet and passing wind break wudu; sleep and loss of consciousness also do, with differences in detail
Cites Bukhari 135: prayer is not accepted from someone whose wudu is broken until they renew it
Says bleeding, vomiting, touching private parts and touching the opposite sex are treated differently by the four schools

faq:faq-pry-015.title: What if I can't use water because of illness, injury or no access?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 5:6 for tayammum when ill, travelling or unable to find water
Says one method uses one strike and wipes the hands to the wrists (Bukhari 338); the Hanafi method uses two strikes and wipes to the elbows
Says you return to wudu or ghusl once you can use water again

faq:faq-pry-016.title: What is the minimum I need to do for ghusl?
keyPoints: Says the minimum ghusl is water reaching the whole body, incl. hair roots, with intention; difference note mentions rinsing mouth and nose
Includes intention in the minimum; check against the Hanafi school, which treats intention in ghusl as sunnah
Describes the Prophet's full method (Bismillah, hands, private parts, wudu, head three times, right then left); only a NewMuslims.com lesson is attached

faq:faq-wor-011.title: Can I make wudu while wearing nail polish?
keyPoints: Says wudu made over regular nail polish does not count because the polish stops water reaching the nails
Says polish applied after wudu does not affect that wudu; remove it before the next wudu

faq:faq-wor-012.title: In winter, can I wipe over my socks instead of washing my feet?
keyPoints: Says socks must go on after a full wudu; wiping lasts one day and night at home, three days and nights when travelling
Says the Hanafi school requires thick socks you could walk in that water does not soak through
Says 'others allow ordinary socks'; confirm which schools or scholars this refers to

faq:faq-wor-013.title: I have a cast, a bandage or a disability. How do I make wudu? What if I cannot use water at all?
keyPoints: Says Hanafi: wipe a part that cannot get wet with a wet hand, else wipe over the cast, else leave it; Shafi'i adds tayammum and sometimes repeats the prayer
Says for ghusl with an injury, catheter or insulin pump the Shafi'i school washes what it can, wipes the rest and adds tayammum
Says the Hanafi school excuses one who cannot pray in any way; the Shafi'i school says prayer is due while the mind is clear, even in the heart
Cites Quran 2:286 and 5:6; says a doctor's advice counts when judging harm

faq:faq-lrn-003.title: Which English translation of the Quran should I read?
keyPoints: Recommends The Clear Quran by Dr. Mustafa Khattab ('a Canadian-Egyptian scholar') and M.A.S. Abdel Haleem's Oxford translation, via Yaqeen's list
Says both translations can be read free on Quran.com
Says square brackets in Saheeh International are the translators' additions

faq:faq-lrn-004.title: How do I learn to read Arabic from zero?
keyPoints: Recommends a Qaida primer (e.g. Qaida Nooraniyah): letters and sounds, joining with short vowels, then short chapters with a teacher
Says New Muslim Academy runs free live small-group classes held separately for men and women; only the sisters' class page is cited
Cites Muslim 798a / Bukhari 4937: the one who struggles with the Quran gets a double reward

faq:faq-lrn-005.title: Do I have to learn tajweed before I read the Quran?
keyPoints: Says tajweed need not be learned before reading; it is learned step by step alongside reading
Advises saying al-Fatihah as clearly as possible by listening to a clear reciter and repeating
Difference note: which pronunciation mistakes affect the prayer is a detail to go through with a teacher

faq:faq-lrn-007.title: Is it okay to read or listen to the Quran in English only for now?
keyPoints: Says reading a translation is good if understood as a translation of the meaning, not the Quran itself
Cites Quran 54:17: the Quran made easy to remember and take lessons from
Suggests reading a short English passage daily and listening to the same passage in Arabic

faq:faq-lrn-010.title: What is tafsir, and do I need it?
keyPoints: Defines tafsir as scholars' explanation: meaning at revelation, how the Prophet and companions understood it, links to other verses
Recommends Yaqeen Institute's free Qur'an 30 for 30 now and classical works like Tafsir Ibn Kathir later

faq:faq-wor-014.title: What actually breaks a fast?
keyPoints: Says eating, drinking and sexual intercourse on purpose between dawn and sunset break the fast
Says many medicines do not break the fast and a needed dose should never be skipped; refers to IIFA Resolution 93 on drops, injections, inhalers
Paraphrases Bukhari 1903: Allah has no need of someone giving up food while still lying and doing wrong
Difference note: schools differ on inhalers, nasal sprays, blood tests and which breaks need expiation

faq:faq-wor-015.title: I forgot I was fasting and ate something. Is my fast ruined?
keyPoints: Says eating or drinking out of true forgetfulness does not break the fast and the day need not be made up
Paraphrases Bukhari 1933 / Muslim 1155: 'Allah fed you and gave you drink'
preCheckFlags: States no make-up is needed, with no difference note; the Maliki school requires a make-up (qada) of an obligatory fast broken by forgetful eating

faq:faq-wor-016.title: Who does not have to fast?
keyPoints: Lists exemptions: illness or travel and menstruation or postnatal bleeding (made up later), pregnant or breastfeeding women fearing harm, children
Says those who can fast only with extreme lasting difficulty (old age, chronic illness) give fidyah instead (Quran 2:184)
Says diabetes alone does not exempt since many fast safely with a medical plan; the Diabetes Canada source lists high-risk groups who should not fast
Difference note: pregnancy and breastfeeding (make-up only or plus fidyah) and travel conditions differ by school

faq:faq-wor-017.title: How do I make up fasts I missed?
keyPoints: Says make up one day per missed day, not necessarily in a row, after Ramadan and before the next one
Says intention is made the night before; difference note calls this Hanafi and Shafi'i, but Maliki and Hanbali also require it for obligatory fasts
Says fasting on the two Eid days is not allowed

faq:faq-wor-018.title: What is fidyah, and how much is it in Canada?
keyPoints: Says fidyah is feeding a person in need for each fast you cannot do or make up later (Quran 2:184)
Says Islamic Relief Canada lists CAD 15 per day for 2026
Distinguishes kaffarah as the much heavier expiation for deliberately breaking a Ramadan fast
Says if you might be able to make the days up later, you usually make them up instead of paying

faq:faq-wor-019.title: This is my first Ramadan and my family does not fast. How do I cope?
keyPoints: Paraphrases Bukhari 1923: the pre-dawn meal (suhoor) has blessing in it
Suggests inviting family to iftar and asking your masjid about community iftars

faq:faq-wor-020.title: What is Laylat al-Qadr and what should I do on it?
keyPoints: Says the Quran calls the night better than a thousand months (97:3), but no Quran 97 source is attached
Says it falls in the last ten nights of Ramadan, its date is hidden, and people make extra effort on the odd nights
Check the dua 'Allahumma innaka afuwwun tuhibbul afwa fa'fu anni' and its translation (Tirmidhi 3513, graded sahih)
